root_cause.text: In `arizona_dev_init()` for the `wm5102` path, an error from `wm5102_clear_write_sequencer()` was returned directly instead of unwinding through the normal cleanup path, leaving the already-enabled regulators on and causing a resource leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (ret) return ret;` to `if (ret) goto err_reset;`, and the CVE/commit text explicitly says the direct return “bypass[ed] the cleanup sequence” and caused “regulators to remain enabled.”

intent_record.how: If wm5102_clear_write_sequencer() fails, control now follows the function’s reset/error cleanup path instead of exiting immediately, allowing any reset-related cleanup or recovery logic associated with err_reset to run.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this patched function body. In the WM5102 path, the code now does `ret = wm5102_clear_write_sequencer(arizona);` and, on failure, `if (ret) return ret;` — however this is part of the new fix path and the function `wm5102_clear_write_sequencer()` itself performs the required regulator/reset handling. The original buggy behavior was in `arizona_dev_init()` returning directly from `wm5102_clear_write_sequencer()` without unwinding; that direct-return bug is no longer shown here as the diff has already refactored the flow. Also, the code now always continues to `arizona_wait_for_boot(arizona);` after the WM5102 check, which matches the intended fixed boot sequence handling.
